title: Surface Areas and Volumes: Cones and Spheres

standard_code: Class 9, Chapter 11: Surface Areas and Volumes
standard_text: Surface areas and volumes of spheres (including hemispheres) and right circular cones (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 9 Surface Areas and Volumes worksheet (NCERT Chapter 11): slant height, curved and total surface area of cones, spheres and hemispheres, and their volumes. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Cone: πrl and ⅓πr²h; sphere: 4πr² and 4/3 πr³
body_html:
How it works

Cone (radius r, height h, slant height l = √(r² + h²)): curved surface πrl, total surface πr(l + r), volume ⅓πr²h.

Sphere: surface 4πr², volume 4/3 πr³. Hemisphere: curved surface 2πr², total surface 3πr², volume ⅔πr³.

Use π = 22/7 when the radius is a multiple of 7. 1 m³ = 1,000 litres and 1,000 cm³ = 1 litre.

Example

A cone has r = 7 cm and h = 24 cm. Find its curved surface area.

l = √(49 + 576) = 25

πrl = 22/7 × 7 × 25

Answer: 550 cm²

Example

Find the volume of a sphere of radius 21 cm.

4/3 × 22/7 × 21³

Answer: 38,808 cm³

Common mistakes

  • Using the height h in πrl. The curved surface uses the slant height l.
  • Forgetting ⅓ in the volume of a cone.
  • Using 4πr² for a hemisphere. Its curved surface is 2πr²; a solid hemisphere has 3πr² in all.

faq.q: What is the curved surface area of a cone?
faq.a: πrl, where r is the base radius and l = √(r² + h²) is the slant height.

faq.q: What is the volume of a cone?
faq.a: ⅓πr²h, one third of a cylinder with the same base and height.

faq.q: What is the surface area of a sphere?
faq.a: 4πr². A hemisphere has curved surface 2πr² and, if solid, total surface 3πr².

faq.q: What is the volume of a sphere and a hemisphere?
